text: Why is the ocean salty, but rivers aren't?
Rainwater is slightly acidic, so over time, it slowly breaks down rocks on land.
That frees tiny amounts of minerals, and rivers carry them to the sea.
Rivers taste fresh because the amounts are tiny. But the ocean collects them.
The sun evaporates the water, the salt stays behind, and over millions of years, it added up.
Vents on the seafloor add even more minerals from inside the Earth.
Today, every liter of seawater holds about thirty-five grams of salt.
Spread over all the land, that salt would make a layer as tall as a forty-story building.
Would you have guessed that much?
